title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer regional failover race condition
author: Evan Chen
description:
Summary: This hotfix addresses a race condition in the SLO enforcer that could cause duplicate regional failover and aggressive load-shedding during transient controller flaps. The race manifested when two region controllers simultaneously believed the other was unhealthy and both initiated failover; this occasionally led to over-shedding and client-visible errors (observed during the 2025-10-19 incident referenced in SUP-5421).

Root cause: state transition in the enforcer was not serialized across regions when the controller observed near-simultaneous SLO breaches. We used in-memory heuristics and an immediate broadcast model which could result in both regions proceeding with failover before either updated the shared controller state in the metadata store.

What this change does:
- Introduces a lightweight compare-and-swap (CAS) based guard on the central metadata key for region failover intent to serialize leader transitions.
- Adds a short jittered backoff when a CAS failure is observed to avoid thundering retries under contention.
- Verifies in-flight request counters against a configurable threshold before escalating to full regional failover (prevents failover for localized bursts).
- Adds explicit metrics and tracing for CAS failures and enforced backoffs to aid future debugging.
- Includes unit and integration tests that reproduce the race and assert deterministic outcome.

Rollout plan: cut hotfix -> canary two pods in us-west -> monitor slo_enforcer.failover_count and slo_enforcer.cas_failures for 2 hours -> ramp to 20% -> full roll. Post-merge we patched the production canary (observability dashboard updated).

Testing: added deterministic race repro test (services/slo-enforcer/test/regional_failover_race_test.go) and increased coverage around decision logic. CI initially failed due to a flaky test in the decision tree; I stabilized the test by seeding the RNG and adding a small time tolerance. Full suite: unit + integration + e2e (canary) passed on final run.

Checklist:
- [x] Repro case and incident reference added (SUP-5421)
- [x] CAS guard implemented and unit-tested
- [x] Backoff & jitter implemented and metrics instrumented
- [x] Integration test simulates dual-controller failover scenario
- [x] Reviewed by runtime/reliability engineers
- [x] Canary rollout completed and monitored

Notes: This is intentionally conservative (adds a single metadata CAS and short backoff) to minimize blast radius. We debated a leader-election redesign but chose this pragmatic hotfix to stabilize the fleet while keeping the longer-term refactor tracked under ENG-3142.
